name: Rosemary Chicken Thighs

ingredients.buy: 2 lb 10 oz Brussels sprouts, ends trimmed and halved
3 1/2 medium yellow onions, thinly sliced (about 5 1/4 cups)
3 1/2 medium tart apples such as Granny Smith, halved, cored, and cut into 8 wedges each
7 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, divided
8 3/4 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 17 large thighs)
18 sprigs fresh rosemary, plus chopped fresh rosemary for serving

prose.intro_html:
Here is a sheet pan that does the whole job while you do nothing. Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs go down on the same tray as Brussels sprouts, sliced onion, and tart apple wedges, and the oven sorts them out. The apples go soft and sweet, the sprouts and onions darken and crisp where the honey caramelizes, and the chicken skin turns gold under a two-minute broil. Fresh rosemary lays across the top and perfumes the whole thing.

The numbers are honest: {{cal}} calories a serving with {{protein}} grams of protein and only 19.7 grams of carbohydrate. That is a dinner that fills the container and keeps its promises. Thighs are the thrifty cook's cut for a reason. They cost less than breasts, they stay juicy when you are cooking seventeen of them at once, and the skin is where all the flavor lives.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the thighs bone-in and skin-on. That is the cheapest way chicken comes and it is the version this recipe wants, because the skin crisps and the bone keeps the meat from drying out across a big batch. A family pack is your friend here; you need close to nine pounds, so grab the biggest tray the case has rather than three small ones.

Brussels sprouts on the stalk or loose in a bag both work. Loose in a bag lets you pick through and skip the yellowed ones. Any tart, firm apple does the job, and Granny Smith is the classic pick because it holds up to heat before it collapses into that jammy layer under the chicken.

Dijon, honey, olive oil, kosher salt, black pepper, and fresh rosemary are pantry and produce-aisle staples you likely keep on hand. Fresh rosemary comes in a clamshell that gives you plenty of sprigs; you need eighteen for the pan plus a little chopped for the finish, so one package covers the batch with room to spare.
prose.make_it:
Set two oven racks, one in the center and one in the upper third, and heat the oven to 425F. You want both because the chicken bakes low-and-center, then finishes with a broil up top.

On a large rimmed sheet pan, pile the sliced onion, apple wedges, and halved Brussels sprouts in the middle. Top them with 1 tablespoon of the oil, the honey, the Dijon, half the salt, and half the pepper. Toss to coat and spread it all in an even layer.

Nestle the chicken onto the pan skin side up, pushing the fruit and veg aside so each thigh sits right on the metal. Pat the skin dry, season with the remaining salt and pepper, drizzle the last tablespoon of oil over the top, and lay a rosemary sprig across each piece. If you run short on sprigs, snap them into pieces and spread them around.

Bake on the center rack for 15 minutes. Pull the pan, stir the vegetables with a spatula, and return it for another 5 to 10 minutes, until the chicken reads 165F at the thickest part on an instant-read thermometer. If some thighs finish first, move them to a plate and let the rest catch up. The apples will break down soft and the sprouts and onions will darken and crisp as the honey caramelizes.

Take out the pan, discard the spent rosemary sprigs, and return any chicken you set aside. Switch the oven to broil, move the pan to the upper rack, and broil 2 to 3 minutes until the skin is golden and crackling. If you would rather the veg not crisp further, lift them off first or broil the chicken on a separate lined pan.

Finish with a pinch of salt and a scatter of chopped fresh rosemary, and serve the chicken hot with the apples and vegetables.
prose.portion_html: This batch fills 14 containers. The clean way to split it is to weigh the empty container, then weigh it again as you build each one and stop at the same number every time. Give each container one to two thighs depending on their size, since seventeen thighs across fourteen boxes means most get one big piece and a few get a smaller second, then an even share of the caramelized sprouts, onion, and soft apple. Aim for the same total weight in every box and the macros hold at {{cal}} calories, {{protein}} grams of protein, and 19.7 grams of carbohydrate a serving.
prose.cost_closing_html: Bone-in thighs and sheet-pan vegetables are about as cheap as a real dinner gets, and this one lands at {{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a full plate of protein, roasted vegetables, and fruit for less than a drive-through combo, cooked fourteen at a time on one pan you only wash once.
prose.upsell_html: Fourteen dinners, one sheet pan, {{cost_ps}} each. Cook it Sunday and you have eaten well every night this week without thinking about it once. If you want the whole system of eating like this for the price of a coffee, membership is a dollar a month.
